message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported its third fiscal quarter ended 2026-07-31 with revenue of $1.85 billion, up 36.54 per cent from a year earlier, and net income of $397 million, up 107.85 per cent [D1]. Gross margin was 65.87 per cent and net margin was 21.51 per cent [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group grew revenue 43.09 per cent to $1.35 billion and operating income 86.18 per cent to $458 million, while the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group grew revenue 21.60 per cent to $501 million and operating income 68.48 per cent to $155 million [D1]. Management guided the fourth fiscal quarter to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, about 37 per cent growth at the mid-point, and earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on approximately 172 million diluted shares [D1]. The balance sheet carried total assets of $11.92 billion and stockholders' equity of $6.57 billion [D1].

The bull argument is that demand is now the story, with momentum from the first half continuing as the AI infrastructure ecosystem scales, wireline orders more than doubling from a year earlier and wireline revenue exceeding wireless revenue [D3]. The quarter comfortably exceeded expectations for both earnings and revenue, and the outlook came in above Wall Street forecasts [D2]. The bear argument is that supply, not demand, governs revenue, with management describing a supply environment less flexible than a year earlier and calling the supply chain the governor of near-term revenue conversion [D3]. Management also cautioned that one-time tariff impacts this year lifted profitability and will not repeat [D3]. Analysts pressed on the sustainability of demand and on whether the outlook is capped by supply [D3]. Sell-side price targets imply further upside for the shares, though such targets are often set for reasons other than a genuine view of where the stock will trade [D5].

The plan is therefore to own the AI infrastructure test intensity theme, since shrinking design margins force customers to test at the signal, bit and protocol levels in research and development and in production [D4]. Position size should respect the supply governor, with revenue conversion expected to be nonlinear over the next several quarters [D3]. The next report is the test: fourth-quarter revenue must land in the $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion range with earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 [D1]. Evidence that component supply is loosening enough to convert the pipeline would confirm the thesis, while revenue below the low end of the guided range would disconfirm it [D1]. A separate test is whether margins hold without the tariff benefit that flattered fiscal 2026, where earnings per share below $3.34 would disconfirm [D1]. Management's upcoming investor conference appearances are the nearest scheduled opportunity for an update on supply and on the year ahead [D6]. The research collaboration on AI safety assurance for software-defined vehicles is a reminder that the automotive franchise is being developed alongside communications [D7].
